frame: ORIGINAL scene 04 (配送ネットワーク / the coverage map) settled hold = JourneyPort._scenes.network(80, t) with t starting at 80/30 = 2.6667 s and advancing in real seconds (hero-glue.js, STOPS[3] iStart = 80/30, sec: true). Source: C:/Users/RTX4070TI/Desktop/sanpou-hero-remake/original/js/hero-port-b.js, sceneNetwork lines 1679-1903, CoverageMap lines 1081-1143, map data JRMAP in hero-port-a.js line 3. Stage 1920x1080, origin top-left. THERE IS NO CAMERA AND NO PARALLAX IN THIS SCENE: nothing is translated by a camera, every y and x below is already a screen (stage) pixel. The scene's own ground line is y = 1008/1010 (city base) — but see the next sentence, because at this moment none of that ground is visible. THE ONE FACT THAT GOVERNS THE WHOLE PICTURE: the entire daylight city — sun, clouds, birds, Fuji, all three building tiers, Tokyo Tower, the airport and its plane, the office block, the road and its mini trucks — is wrapped in ONE group, h('g', { opacity: recede }, ...) at line 1736, and recede = interpolate(frame, [86, 112], [0, 1], extrapolateLeft 'clamp'). At frame 80 recede = 0, so that group's opacity is EXACTLY 0 and 554 of the scene's 709 nodes paint nothing. The city only fades UP as the map fades DOWN, during frames 86-112, which belongs to scene 05. Confirmed by pixel probe on a Chromium render of the hold: the stage at the Tokyo Tower top (1350,190) reads 118,186,229; at the Fuji peak (380,460) 148,200,234; at the office (900,960) 174,203,222; at the road (300,1030) 189,217,232; at the sun (1700,120) 99,173,220 — all of them plain sky plus halo plus vignette, no art. So the visible picture at the hold is only FOUR things: the sky gradient, one very soft white halo ellipse, the coverage map in its masked box, and the vignette. All boxes below are SCREEN px as x, y, w, h (or x-range / y-range where clearer), computed by running the unchanged files in Node with a fake window (hero-flag.js sets JX_CLEAN_HERO = true, hero-port-a.js gives JRMAP) and walking the returned {t,a,c} tree with transform composition, then reproducing the inner SVG's viewBox fit by hand, and checked against a Chromium render of the same moment (0 console errors). Node counts: 709 nodes in the whole scene, of which 104 are the CoverageMap subtree (the only part you can see), 554 are the invisible background group, and the rest are the sky/halo/star/wrapper scaffolding. Scene function cost about 0.42 ms/frame in Node (no DOM) — a third of scene 01's, because almost all of the node count is static map paths. Player facts: scene 04 runs 21800-27800 ms on the site clock (viewer/timeline.js: scene 03 = 14600-21800, scene 04 = 21800-27800, scene 05 = 27800-45800); the entrance plays frames 0 -> 80 at ENTER_RATE 1.2 (36 frames/s) = 2222.2 ms, so the hold begins at 24022 ms and lasts 3778 ms, with ambient t running 2.6667 -> 6.4444 s. The 03 -> 04 change is a CROSSFADE done by the player, not by the scene: hero-glue.js holds the outgoing scene-03 picture at opacity 1 for one frame (33 ms) and then fades it out over 850 ms with cubic-bezier(.2,.6,.2,1), so for the first ~0.9 s of scene 04 the expressway gantry, signs and convoy are still visible UNDER the arriving map (clearly seen in the 22400 ms still). Desktop crop centre FOCUS_X[3] = 960; phones blend to CAM_M[3] (x 1015 -> 1015, y 560 -> 550, zoom 1.00 -> 1.03) — the gentlest camera of the five, and that is player camera, not scene art. In stage terms: centre (943, 540), radii 612 x 697; fully opaque out to 355.0 x 404.2; alpha 0.6 at 465.1 x 529.7; alpha 0 at 569.2 x 648.2. Sampled: alpha 1.000 at every label plate and at the hub pin, 0.411 at the Niigata north-west tip (640, 90), 0.582 at the Chiba south tip (1180, 1000), 0.909 at the left edge of the map's viewBox (563, 540), 0.786 at the right edge (1357, 540). The fade is visible on the render: the top of Niigata reads 211,179,160 against its full-strength 230,179,149 lower down. The svg inside is overflow:hidden, so anything the map draws outside 535-1385 / 12-1068 is clipped — but the grey land has already faded to alpha 0.03 or less by then, so the clip edge is never seen.

elements.name: Covered prefectures — each one (JRMAP.covered order = paint order)

Tokyo is the smallest of the eight (202 x 103 px) and carries the hub pin. Nothing hides any prefecture — they tile without overlap. The only partial fade is the wrapper mask at the far ends: Niigata's north-west tip drops to alpha 0.41 and Chiba's southern peninsula to 0.58.

elements.name: Routes — shared look
elements.layer: 9 map, painted over the prefectures and under the labels
elements.screenBox: 7 straight lines, all starting at the Itabashi hub (1050.4, 781.4)
elements.look: AnimatedRoute (769-775): a straight stroked path with round caps. While it is still drawing it uses strokeDasharray = length length with a shrinking offset, so it reads as a SOLID line growing outward; once draw reaches 1 it switches to strokeDasharray '3.5 11' with a negative, time-driven dashoffset, so it becomes a trail of short dashes flowing from the hub outwards. Stroke 3.2 map units = 5.2 px, dashes 5.7 px long with 18.0 px gaps, opacity 0.8. Against the warm prefecture fills the vermilion is only a little lighter than the land, so the routes read as a soft dotted suggestion rather than a graphic line — the long ones (Niigata, Tochigi, Gunma) read clearly because they cross the pale northern shapes, the short ones (Saitama, Kanagawa) almost disappear. The routes go hub -> centroid as the crow flies; there is no road shape, no curve and no arrowhead.

ambientMotion.what: Route flow dashes (the main visible motion of the hold)
ambientMotion.formula: strokeDashoffset = -(flowTime * 22) map units, flowTime = the ambient clock in seconds; strokeDasharray '3.5 11' (5.7 px dash, 18.0 px gap). The dash pattern therefore crawls outward from the hub at 22 map units/s = 35.9 stage px/s, one dash cycle every 0.659 s. At t = 2.6667 the offset is -58.67, at t = 6.4444 it is -141.78. SIX routes flow (Chiba, Ibaraki, Tochigi, Gunma, Niigata, Kanagawa); the SAITAMA route does not, because its draw never reaches 1 and it stays a static solid line.

two circles, pp = (flowTime * 0.45 + j * 0.5) % 1 for j = 0, 1; r = 13 + pp * 30 map units = 21.2 -> 70.2 px; opacity = pinE * (1 - pp) * 0.55, so each ring starts bright and small and fades as it grows. Period 2.222 s, the two rings 1.111 s apart.

pp = (flowTime * 0.5 + j * 0.4) % 1 (j = 0 Shiki, j = 1 Iruma); r = 10 + pp * 7 map units = 16.3 -> 27.7 px; opacity = (1 - pp) * 0.35. Period 2 s, the two 0.8 s out of phase. Much smaller and fainter than the hub's.

ambientMotion.what: Everything else that is visible is frozen
ambientMotion.formula: Diffing network(80, t) against network(80, t + 3.37) changes 117 nodes, but 107 of them are inside the background group at opacity 0. The 10 that are actually visible are exactly the 6 flowing routes, the 2 base-marker rings and the 2 hub rings. The prefecture shapes, the grey land, all 8 label plates, both badges, the pin body, the sky, the halo and the vignette do not move at all. The hold is close to a still image — the whole picture has about 100 px of travelling dash and four breathing rings in it, which is the single biggest gap against the reference film's 'the world is never fully frozen' rule.
ambientMotion.sourceLines: chor.cjs / chor.txt in the scratch folder

ambientMotion.what: Niigata's last hundredth (a measurable but invisible residual)
ambientMotion.formula: prefProgress saturates at 1 from frame 56, but Niigata's reveal is k = clamp01((1 - 7*0.055) * 1.5) = 0.9225, e = easeOutCubic(k) = 0.99953. So its group keeps a translate(0, 0.00419) map units (0.007 px) offset and its path stays at opacity 0.9795 instead of 0.98 for the whole scene. Visually nothing; worth knowing when diffing frames.

ambientMotion.what: AMBIENT MOTION THAT EXISTS BUT CANNOT BE SEEN (all inside the opacity-0 city group)
ambientMotion.formula: Sun glow r = 190 + 24*(0.5+0.5*sin(0.55t)) and its opacity 0.7 + 0.3*pulse, period 11.42 s. Five clouds: wx = ((sp*t*4 + i*560) % 2400) - 240 at 40.0 / 28.0 / 48.0 / 22.0 / 16.8 px/s, with a vertical bob sin(0.4t + 1.7i)*6 px and an edge fade over the first and last 210 px. Three birds drifting, bobbing (sin(0.7t + 2.2i)*9) and flapping (sin(7t + 1.9i)*3.4). Tokyo Tower tip beacon, opacity 0.2 + 0.8*(0.5+0.5*sin(pi*t)), period 2 s. Airport: control-tower lamp 0.3 + 0.7*(0.5+0.5*sin(3.2t)) period 1.96 s, radar sweep (t*46) % 360 = one turn every 7.83 s, windsock rotating sin(1.7t)*7 deg. Three mini trucks sliding and spinning their wheels. The airport plane on its 19 s cycle. All of it is computed every frame and multiplied by 0.

ambientMotion.what: Player camera on narrow viewports only (outside the scene function)
ambientMotion.formula: Desktop: a static crop centred on stage x 960. As the window narrows (mobT = clamp((1500 - boxW/scale)/880)) the crop blends toward CAM_M[3]: centre x 1015 -> 1015, y 560 -> 550, zoom 1.00 -> 1.03 across the 6 s dwell, eased in-out and exponentially smoothed (rate 2.6/s). This is the flattest camera move of the five scenes — on a phone the map barely drifts. Reduced motion pins it at the midpoint.

choreography.what: The 03 -> 04 change is a crossfade run by hero-glue.js, not by sceneNetwork: the outgoing scene-03 picture stays at opacity 1 for one frame (33 ms) and then fades out over 850 ms with cubic-bezier(.2,.6,.2,1). So during frames 0-31 of scene 04 the expressway gantry, the green signs and the four Sanpou trucks are still visible UNDER the arriving map (clearly readable in the 22400 ms still). The incoming map is NOT hidden during this — the two pictures are simply stacked.

The map box eases in: opacity 0 -> 1 with easeOutCubic, scale 0.95 -> 1.00, and translateY (1 - mapIn) * 34 px, so it rises 34 px while it fades up, about transform-origin (926, 497.8). Values: f0 0.000 / 0.950 / 34.0 px, f4 0.394 / 0.970 / 20.6, f8 0.668 / 0.983 / 11.3, f13 0.875 / 0.994 / 4.3, f18 0.971 / 0.999 / 1.0, f22 0.996 / 1.000 / 0.1, f26 1.000 / 1.000 / 0.0. The grey land, which is part of the same box, comes up with it.

choreography.frames: 4-56 (prefs) — the prefectures reveal outward from the hub
choreography.what: prefProgress = clamp01((frame - 4) / 52). Each prefecture's own k = clamp01((prefProgress - rank*0.055) * 1.5), e = easeOutCubic(k); the shape rises (1-e)*9 map units (14.7 px) and fades in at opacity e*0.98, so they drop into place one after another. REVEAL_RANK is by straight-line distance from the Itabashi hub, computed at runtime: 0 TOKYO (20.5 units), 1 SAITAMA (56.3), 2 KANAGAWA (63.2), 3 CHIBA (69.0), 4 IBARAKI (119.7), 5 TOCHIGI (137.3), 6 GUNMA (140.5), 7 NIIGATA (265.9). So the colour spreads from Tokyo outward like ink. Reveal e by rank at f8: 0.31 0.10 0 0 0 0 0 0 | f13: 0.59 0.44 0.26 0.04 0 0 0 0 | f18: 0.79 0.69 0.56 0.40 0.21 0 0 0 | f22: 0.89 0.82 0.73 0.61 0.47 0.29 0.07 0 | f26: 0.95 0.91 0.85 0.77 0.66 0.53 0.36 0.16 | f34: 1.00 0.99 0.97 0.94 0.90 0.84 0.75 0.64 | f46: all >= 0.95 | f56: all 1.00 (except Niigata's 0.99953 forever). The 8 label plates fade in on exactly the same e, so each name arrives with its prefecture.

routeProgress = clamp01((frame - 34) / 44); route i draws with draw = clamp01((routeProgress - i*0.07) * 1.7), staggered 0.07 apart in ROUTE_ORDER (Chiba, Ibaraki, Tochigi, Gunma, Niigata, Kanagawa, Saitama). While draw < 1 the line is SOLID and grows from the hub (dasharray = length length, offset = length*(1-draw)); its opacity ramps as 0.8 * min(1, draw*3), so it is already at full strength by draw 0.33. The moment draw hits 1 it flips to the flowing '3.5 11' dash — a visible change of texture, line by line. draw by route at f40: 0.23 0.11 0 0 0 0 0 | f46: 0.46 0.34 0.23 0.11 0 0 0 | f52: 0.70 0.58 0.46 0.34 0.22 0.10 0 | f56: 0.85 0.73 0.61 0.49 0.37 0.25 0.14 | f60: 1.00 0.89 0.77 0.65 0.53 0.41 0.29 (Chiba is the first to flip) | f64: 1.00 1.00 0.92 0.80 0.68 0.56 0.45 | f68: 1.00 1.00 1.00 0.96 0.84 0.72 0.60 | f72: 1.00 1.00 1.00 1.00 0.99 0.87 0.75 | f76: 1.00 x6, 0.91 | f78 and after: 1.00 x6, 0.9898 — Saitama is stuck one hundredth short and never flips.

pinProgress = clamp01((frame - 60) / 18). The HUB pin group fades in at easeOutCubic(pinProgress) and its body scales by pop = 1 + 0.22*sin(min(1,pinProgress)*pi) times 0.82, i.e. it overshoots by up to 22% and settles: pop 1.14 at f64, 1.22 at f68 (the peak), 1.19 at f72, 1.08 at f76, 1.00 at f78. Markers 2 and 3 come in later and staggered: e = easeOutCubic(clamp01(pinProgress*1.3 - 0.25 - j*0.15)), with a bigger bounce of 1 + 0.28*sin(e*pi). Shiki e: 0.11 at f64, 0.70 at f68, 0.94 at f72, 1.00 at f76. Iruma e: 0 at f64, 0.44 at f68, 0.85 at f72, 0.99 at f76, 1.00 at f78 (it is still 0.9999 at f80). The pulse rings start as soon as the groups appear.

The map is fully drawn: 8 prefectures at opacity 0.98, 8 label plates, 6 flowing routes plus the stuck Saitama line, 3 pins with their rings. The city behind is at opacity 0, so the frame is sky + halo + map + vignette. Ambient time continues from 80/30 = 2.6667 s and runs to 6.4444 s over the 3778 ms hold. Nothing but the dashes and the four rings moves.

choreography.frames: 4-36 and 86-104 (overlay timings that exist in code but draw nothing)
choreography.what: titleEnter ramps 0 -> 1 over frames 4-36 and back down from frame 86, and basesEnter / overviewEnter are springs released at frames 14 and 26 — all computed, all discarded, because SceneTitle and KpiCard return null under JX_CLEAN_HERO.

choreography.frames: after 80 (belongs to scene 05, for context only)
choreography.what: 86-112 (mapRecede): the map fades and pulls back — opacity 1 -> 0, scale 1.00 -> 0.92, translateX 0 -> -36 px — while the SAME group's inverse, the city, fades up from opacity 0 to 1. recede by frame: f92 0.049, f99 0.500, f105 0.922, f112 1.000. At about frame 106 (recede >= 0.96) the empty KPI wrapper div is dropped from the tree and the vignette moves from child index 4 to index 3. 96-126 logo reveal, 116-140 tagline, 128-174 stats — all null under the flag. The site plays frames 80 -> 174 as scene 05's entrance and then holds at 174.

disabledOrHidden: THE WHOLE DAYLIGHT CITY. h('g', { opacity: recede }) at line 1736 wraps the sun, 26 stars, the shooting star, the lower halo, 5 clouds, 3 birds, Mt Fuji, 15 CITY_DEEP buildings, the horizon haze, Tokyo Tower, 6 CITY_BACK and 4 CITY_FRONT buildings, the wide sun glow, the airport, the office block, the road and its 3 mini trucks and the airport plane — 554 of the scene's 709 nodes — and at frame 80 recede is 0. None of it is visible, and pixel probes on the render confirm plain sky everywhere it would be. It is listed in full under elements because the remake has to draw it for scene 05 and because the 04 -> 05 move is this group coming up as the map goes down.

KpiCard '主要拠点 / OUR BASES' (x 1290, y 140, width 540, listing 板橋本社・倉庫 HQ, 志木営業所, 入間営業所 with their addresses) and KpiCard 'ネットワーク概況 / NETWORK OVERVIEW' (x 1290, y 584, three counters 3 物流拠点 / 7 対応都県 / 32台 保有車両): both return null under JX_CLEAN_HERO (864-866). Only the empty wrapper div at line 1865 remains, with its opacity and translateX animated for nothing. The bob values Math.sin(time*1.1)*5 and Math.sin(time*1.1+1.4)*5 are computed and discarded. NOTE the facts in that dead code — 3 bases, 7 prefectures, 32 vehicles — if the remake ever wants them on screen, that is an owner decision, not a drawing one.

SceneTitle for the network scene (CONTENT.scenes.network, line 1894): returns null under the flag and leaves no wrapper div at all — unlike scene 01, which leaves two empty divs. titleEnter is still computed from frames 4-36 and 86-104.
The logo / tagline / eyebrow block (1895-1900, LogoReveal 1030-1051): gated on frame >= T_NETWORK.logo[0] - 2 (94) AND !window.JX_CLEAN_HERO, so it never renders in this build at any frame.

The map legend (1135-1141): 'window.JX_CLEAN_HERO ? null : ...' — the 172 x 46 dark plate with the two swatches 配送対応エリア and 営業エリア外 that would sit at map (229, 858.7) = stage (599.4, 911.2) is never drawn. legendE is still computed at line 1086.
FloatingParticles({ seed: 'network', 28 motes over 80,120,1760,840 }) at line 1735: the function's first statement is 'return null' (675), so no node exists.
The 30 star circles at lines 1730-1734 and the 26 star circles at 1755-1759: all written with opacity: 0. Their random positions and twinkle values are computed every frame.
The shooting star at lines 1760-1767: the body begins 'var k = (time % 9) / 9; if (true) return null;' — dead code for a streak that would fly from (1480,70) to (1180,200).
The sun's 12 rays at lines 1742-1750: the loop builds the whole path string d and then 'return null'. The scene-04 sun has no rays, exactly like scene 01's.

The empty group at lines 1725-1728: h('g', { opacity: 0.5 - recede*0.3 }) with no children at all — two blank source lines where its contents were removed. It still occupies child index 1 of the SVG and still gets its opacity attribute rewritten as recede changes.

The SAITAMA route never completes: draw = clamp01((1 - 6*0.07)*1.7) = 0.9898 at best, so it stays in the un-flowed branch for the entire scene — a SOLID vermilion line ending 1.3 px short of the Saitama centroid instead of the flowing dashes the other six get. On screen it is a faint lighter streak from the hub up-left towards 埼玉 (see shots/crop-saitama-route.png). Treat it as a bug to fix, not a look to copy.

NIIGATA never reaches full opacity: its reveal e tops out at 0.99953, so its fill sits at 0.9795 rather than 0.98 and its group keeps a 0.007 px drop. Invisible, but it means the scene never reaches a truly settled state.

Cloud #4 (wx 2044.8 at the start of the hold) is off the right edge of the stage even before the group's opacity is applied; cloud #0 (wx -133.3) is half off the left edge. CITY_DEEP #14 (x 1826-1922) runs 2 px past the right edge.

Grey-land paths that fall outside the map box: of the 24 paths, #0, #1, #2, #3, #4 and #14, #17, #18, #19, #20, #21, #22, #23 lie wholly or mostly outside the wrapper div (stage x -279..1545, y -694..1381) and are clipped by its overflow:hidden. In practice the landFade mask has already taken them to alpha 0.03 or less before the clip edge, so the clip is never visible — but they are real nodes with real cost (33,636 characters of path data for the greys against 8,408 for the eight coloured prefectures).

Nothing in the map hides anything else: the eight prefectures tile without overlap, no label plate is covered, and all three pins sit on top. The only 'hiding' in the scene is the wrapper mask's edge fade — Niigata's north-west tip at alpha 0.41 and Chiba's southern peninsula at alpha 0.58 — and the landFade gradient on the grey land.

The left and right 535 px of the stage, and the band above y 74 and below y 1006 outside the map's shapes, hold NOTHING but sky, the halo ellipse and the vignette. Over half the frame is empty at this moment. That emptiness is the scene's biggest opportunity in the remake, and also the reason the original's 04 reads as a slide rather than a shot.

Positional-diff hazard: the KPI wrapper div is a conditional null (recede < 0.96 ? div : null, line 1865). It is present for frames 0-105 and absent from about frame 106, so the root's child list shrinks from 5 to 4 and the vignette shifts index. Keep node lists stable in the remake, as CLAUDE.md warns.
